name: Li Zhijun
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Double Medical Technology Inc. (大博医疗, SZSE: 002901); Chairman, Double Medical International Investment Co. (HK)
profile: 林志军 (romanised Lin Zhijun; listed here as 'Li') co-founded Xiamen-based orthopaedic implant maker Double Medical with his brother, chairman Lin Zhixiong, and has been vice chairman since 2004. The brothers jointly control the company; he directly holds ~19.5% (2025 annual report). Born Sept 1975, Chinese national with HK permanent residency.
interesting_fact: The company describes the founding duo as complementary: elder brother Lin Zhixiong is a former orthopaedic surgeon, while Lin Zhijun brought front-line medical-device sales and management experience.
deep_cut_fact: Before Double Medical, he ran Xiamen Inet Medical Devices (厦门伊耐特医疗器械) as executive director and GM from 1999 to 2008; since 2013 he has been president of the Xiamen Medical Device Association and is a council member of the Xiamen Double Medical Charity Foundation.
notes: Input name 'Li Zhijun' is a romanisation error: 林志军 = Lin Zhijun. Low public profile; best route is via company board secretary / IR email.

name: Zhang Feng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang XCC Group (浙江五洲新春集团, SSE: 603667); controlling shareholder
profile: Zhang Feng (张峰, b. July 1963) built Xinchang-based XCC from a local bearing works into a listed maker of bearings, automotive components and precision parts with plants in Zhejiang, Anhui, Sichuan, Dalian and Mexico. XCC listed in Shanghai in 2016; he is controlling shareholder, chairman and GM, and the firm is now pushing into robot bearings and planetary roller screws for humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: XCC has moved into 'embodied-AI' hardware: its 2025 annual report lists planetary roller screws, ball screws and micro screws for humanoid robots alongside a full range of robot-specific bearings.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1981 as Communist Youth League secretary at the Xinchang Bearing General Factory, later served as deputy head of Xinchang's foreign-trade bureau (1992-98) before running Zhejiang Xinchun Bearing; he is vice chairman of the China Bearing Industry Association.
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via XCC filings (Forbes profile matches XCC). Route via board secretary Peng Yaohui's office (securities dept email above).

name: Li Bogang
current_role: Founder and head of Chengdu Diao Group (成都地奥集团), pharmaceuticals (latest confirmed role as of 2014 reporting)
profile: Li Bogang (李伯刚) was a Chinese Academy of Sciences researcher who in 1988 left to commercialise his own research, founding Chengdu Diao Group around a steroidal-saponin herbal heart medicine (Diao Xinxuekang). By end-2013 the group had ~RMB5bn in assets and >RMB2bn annual output. He has not appeared on Hurun lists since 2013 and recent news on him is scarce.
interesting_fact: In March 2012 Diao Xinxuekang capsules were authorised in the EU (via the Netherlands), reported as the first Chinese therapeutic drug with Chinese IP to enter a developed-country mainstream market.
deep_cut_fact: He started Diao in 1988 with a RMB500,000 loan, renting a corner of the old library of the CAS Chengdu branch; his management motto is '聚财先聚人，聚人先聚心' (to gather wealth, first gather people; to gather people, first win hearts). (People's Daily, 4 Apr 2014, p.20)
notes: Private, unlisted group; little recent coverage, current role and status (incl. alive) could not be confirmed post-2014. Company site is a legacy Flash page with no published contact email.

name: Ding Shizhe
current_role: Director (employee-representative) and Assistant to the Chairman, Betta Pharmaceuticals (贝达药业, SZSE: 300558); GM of Qiyuan Bio (Hangzhou)
profile: Ding Shizhe (丁师哲, b. May 1991) is the son of Betta Pharmaceuticals founder Ding Lieming, maker of Conmana (icotinib), China's first home-grown small-molecule lung-cancer targeted drug; Hurun lists the family's stake jointly. A Saint Louis University graduate (biochemistry + economics), he joined Betta and rose through strategic partnerships to the board in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: He handles Betta's in-licensing and business development: he pushed through the MCLA-129 and ensartinib projects, struck partnerships with InventisBio and Agenus, and led Betta's equity investment in US cancer-drug developer Xcovery.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Saint Louis University in the US with a combined biochemistry-and-economics background, and served as executive deputy GM of 'Betta Dream Factory' (贝达梦工场), the company's incubator platform.
notes: Father-son relationship per media reports of company filings (https://m.jiemian.com/article/14889899.html). Wealth is family-held with Ding Lieming, who is the actual controller. Contact via Betta IR.

name: Sheila Crump Johnson
current_role: Founder and CEO, Salamander Collection (Salamander Hotels & Resorts); Vice Chairman and partner, Monumental Sports & Entertainment
profile: Sheila Johnson (b. 1949, McKeesport, PA) co-founded BET in 1979; its sale to Viacom made her the first Black female billionaire. In 2005 she founded Salamander, whose portfolio includes Salamander Middleburg, Hotel Bennett, Innisbrook, PGA National, Half Moon (Jamaica) and Aspen Meadows. She is a partner in the owner of the Capitals, Wizards and Mystics, and a film producer.
interesting_fact: She published a memoir, 'Walk Through Fire: A Memoir of Love, Loss, and Triumph' (Simon & Schuster), and her first film as producer, 'Kicking It', premiered at Sundance in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: A classically trained violinist (University of Illinois music degree), she taught violin at Sidwell Friends School in DC, then built a private teaching business that raised her income from $7,200 to $64,000 and took students on world tours; at BET she created the show 'Teen Summit'.
notes: Press contact is Matt Owen, VP Communications, Salamander (email published, Cloudflare-obfuscated, on the press page). Instagram listed is the company's, not hers. Very media-friendly; recently widowed (Feb 2026), so be sensitive with timing.

name: Li Jixi
current_role: Founder, Chairman and actual controller, Shanghai WPG Smart Water (上海威派格智慧水务, SSE: 603956)
profile: Li Jixi (李纪玺, b. Oct 1972) has been an entrepreneur since 2002 and built WPG, a Shanghai maker of secondary water-supply pumping equipment and smart-water software for utilities. With his wife Sun Hailing he controls the listed company; he directly holds ~38% (2025 annual report) and remains chairman, with a board term to Dec 2027.
interesting_fact: WPG is a 'smart water' (智慧水务) company: it pairs the pump stations that keep water pressure up in high-rise buildings with digital platforms for city water utilities, and partners with utilities through its subsidiary Shanghai Jieshi Information Technology.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture was Beijing Panda Hengsheng Machinery Equipment (北京熊猫恒盛机械设备), where he was executive director; he holds a CEIBS EMBA and was a member of the Jiading District (Shanghai) CPPCC from 2016 to 2021.
notes: Hurun 'WPG' = 威派格. Low media profile; route via securities affairs dept email.

name: Liu Zhengguo
current_role: Retired (Jan 2025) as Senior Vice President of Beijing OriginWater Technology (碧水源, SZSE: 300070); remains a shareholder
profile: Liu Zhenguo (刘振国, b. 1965; listed here as 'Zhengguo') is a water engineer who joined OriginWater in 2006 as director and GM alongside founder Wen Jianping, then served as vice chairman (2007-2019) as the membrane water-treatment firm grew into one of China's largest sewage/water-reuse companies. After state-owned China Chengxiang (CCCC) took control in 2019-20 he stayed on as VP/SVP until retiring in January 2025.
interesting_fact: OriginWater is known for membrane bioreactor (MBR) water-treatment and reuse technology used in large Chinese municipal plants; Liu briefly doubled as company president (Jun 2017-Feb 2018).
deep_cut_fact: Before business he spent ~20 years as a public water engineer: starting in 1987 at the Miyun County water bureau, then Beijing Water Authority, Beijing Water & Hydropower Technology Center, and deputy head of the Beijing Soil & Water Conservation Station (1999-2006); he is a senior engineer.
notes: Name in Chinese is 刘振国 (Liu Zhenguo). Retired from OriginWater Jan 2025 (2025 annual report); company IR is only an indirect route. Avoid topics around his share auctions/voting-right arrangements.

name: Mao Quanlin
current_role: Director and Vice President, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical Co. (晶盛机电, SZSE: 300316)
profile: Mao Quanlin (毛全林, b. 1970) is a co-founding executive and shareholder of Jingsheng, the Shaoxing-based maker of crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar-grade silicon, semiconductors and silicon carbide. He has been a director and (senior) vice president since 2010, focused on production management; his wealth comes from Jingsheng shares held directly (~0.8%) and through the founders' holding vehicle.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng is a core supplier of the monocrystalline silicon furnaces behind China's solar boom and has expanded into SiC substrates and semiconductor equipment, directly relevant to energy and chip supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: His formal schooling stopped at junior middle school (初中), yet he rose on production-management experience to the board of a high-tech equipment maker and shares a Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology Award (first prize).
notes: Not the controller (Cao Jianwei / Qiu Minxiu are). Low public profile; route via Jingsheng board office. Good fit for an energy-focused show (solar/SiC equipment).

name: Wang Zhongshan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Mokingran Jewellery Group (梦金园黄金珠宝集团, HKEX: 2585)
profile: Wang Zhongshan (王忠善, aged ~62), founded Tianjin-based gold-jewellery maker and retailer Mokingran in 2000 after starting as an apprentice gemstone setter in the 1990s. The company listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024; he holds ~23.7% directly and, with his family, controls ~60%. Rising gold prices lifted the stake into Hurun's China list in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he was named an official inheritor of Shandong Province intangible cultural heritage for gold-jewellery craftsmanship, and was honoured for 'outstanding contribution to the jewellery industry' on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mokingran he worked as an apprentice doing gemstone inlay and processing in the 1990s, and in January 2013 was recognised as Weifang's 'First Folk Art Master' (首届民间工艺大师).
notes: Family business: wife is an executive director and son is general manager. Route via IR email in the 2025 annual report.

name: Hu Boyan
current_role: Director, NHU Holding Group (新和成控股集团), controlling shareholder of Zhejiang NHU Co. (新和成, SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Boyan (胡柏剡) is the brother of NHU chairman Hu Baifan and one of the nine individuals who co-founded Zhejiang NHU in 1999 with the Xinchang Synthetic Chemical Plant. NHU became one of the world's largest makers of vitamins (A, E), methionine and aroma chemicals. He sits on the board of the holding group (~4% holder) and is a top-10 NHU shareholder in his own name (~0.47%, 2026 interim report).
interesting_fact: NHU, born from a small chemical plant in Xinchang county, Zhejiang, grew into a global supplier of feed and nutrition ingredients such as vitamins A and E and methionine.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the nine individual co-founders named in NHU's 1999 incorporation, alongside Zhang Pingyi, Yuan Yizhong, Shi Cheng and others, with Xinchang Synthetic Chemical Plant (renamed NHU Holding Group in Nov 2009).
notes: Very low public profile; brother Hu Baifan is the public face/controller. Route via NHU securities office.

name: Chen Lingfen
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and President, Huafu Fashion Co. (华孚时尚, SZSE: 002042); co-controller with husband Sun Weiting
profile: Chen Lingfen (陈玲芬, b. 1963) co-founded Huafu with Sun Weiting in 1993 and has been vice chairman since, adding the president role in 2009. Huafu is one of the world's largest makers of melange (colour-spun) yarn, supplying major global apparel brands, with large spinning operations in Zhejiang and Xinjiang. She also serves as the company's head of accounting.
interesting_fact: Huafu calls itself one of the world's largest melange-yarn suppliers and says its yarn is a first choice of major global fashion brands; the 'Huafu' mark is a China Well-Known Trademark.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Huafu she spent 1981-1993 as a civil servant and trader in Shaoxing: deputy section chief at the Shaoxing Economic Cooperation Office, then office director and finance manager at Shaoxing Yueling Trading Co.; she later earned a Renmin University EMBA.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Sun Weiting (chairman). Route via board office email. Avoid Xinjiang-cotton controversy in outreach.

name: Robert A Frist Jr
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, HealthStream Inc. (Nasdaq: HSTM)
profile: Robert 'Bobby' Frist Jr. co-founded Nashville-based HealthStream in 1990 and has led it as CEO and chairman ever since, growing it from a dot-com e-learning startup into a SaaS platform for healthcare workforce training, credentialing and scheduling used across US hospitals. His wealth is largely his HealthStream stake. He also chairs Nashville's Entrepreneur Center, which he co-founded.
interesting_fact: He has been CEO of the same public company for 35+ years (since founding in 1990), and was named Ernst & Young's Southeast 'Entrepreneur of the Year'; he is also a former chairman of the Nashville Health Care Council.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2001 interview he said HealthStream 'began about 10 years ago as a concept by myself and Jeff McLaren'; early on the company won a Computerworld Smithsonian Medallion for innovative use of technology, and he studied business (finance, economics, marketing) at Trinity University in San Antonio.
notes: Media contact is Mollie Condra, Head of IR & Communications (per Q3 2026 earnings release). Nashville startup-ecosystem angle (Entrepreneur Center) fits an entrepreneurship podcast well.

name: Jin Liwei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Coco Healthcare Products (可靠股份, SZSE: 301009); controlling shareholder
profile: Jin Liwei (金利伟, b. Nov 1970) founded Hangzhou Qiaozi Paper in 2001, later renamed Hangzhou Coco Healthcare, a maker of disposable hygiene products best known for its own 'Coco/可靠' adult-incontinence brand plus baby diapers and OEM pet pads. Coco listed on ChiNext in 2021; he controls it directly and through Hangzhou Qiaozhi Investment.
interesting_fact: Coco targets China's ageing-population market: its own brand focuses on adult diapers, pull-ups and care pads, and it set up what it calls the industry's first Zhejiang provincial key enterprise research institute for adult-incontinence care products.
deep_cut_fact: Before hygiene products he ran a car-repair business: general manager of Lin'an Qiaozi Auto Repair Co. (1999-2006), and the 'Qiaozi' (侨资) name carried into his first paper company in 2001.
notes: Low media profile. Route via IR email. Hurun listing only in 2021 (post-IPO peak); current wealth likely lower.

name: Robert Mionis
current_role: President, CEO and (since May 2026) Board Chair, Celestica Inc. (NYSE/TSX: CLS); Director, Textron Inc.
profile: Rob Mionis has run Toronto-based Celestica since August 2015, steering the former contract electronics manufacturer into what it now calls 'a global leader in data center infrastructure', supplying AI/cloud networking switches, servers and storage to hyperscalers. The AI-driven rerating of Celestica stock produced his wealth. He became board chair in May 2026 and joined Textron's board in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Under Mionis, Celestica has repositioned around hyperscale data-center hardware (e.g. high-speed networking switches); its March 2026 release describes the company as 'a global leader in data center infrastructure and advanced technology solutions'.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at General Electric, rose to VP of Integrated Supply Chain at Honeywell Aerospace, ran aircraft-engine MRO firm StandardAero as CEO (2006-13), then spent 2013-15 as an operating partner at private-equity firm Pamplona Capital before Celestica.
notes: Highly relevant for a data-center podcast. Route via Celestica Global Communications (media@celestica.com).

name: CV Jacob
current_role: Deceased (died 31 Jan 2021); was founder-chairman of Synthite Group, Kolenchery, Kerala
profile: C.V. Jacob founded Synthite in 1972 after two decades in civil construction, building it into a major producer of spice oleoresins and natural extracts. He died at home near Kolenchery on 31 January 2021, aged 87-88. His son Dr Viju Jacob is managing director of Synthite Industries.
notes: Deceased (sources: https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2021/01/31/synthite-group-chairman-cv-jacob-dies.html ; https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/veteran-industrialist-and-synthite-group-founder-cv-jacob-passes-away-kochi-142524). The business is now run by MD Dr Viju Jacob; https://synthite.com is the company site if the family business is of interest.

name: Hu Yongmei
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Xia Guoxin) of Shenzhen Ellassay Fashion (歌力思, SSE: 603808); supervisor of Ellassay Investment
profile: Hu Yongmei (胡咏梅) and her husband, founder-chairman Xia Guoxin, are joint actual controllers of Ellassay, the Shenzhen-based high-end womenswear group. Beyond its own ELLASSAY label it owns global rights to Laurèl and Paris brand IRO and holds UK brand self-portrait. She was a company director from 2014 to Jan 2021 and is now not on the board; she keeps a low profile.
interesting_fact: Ellassay has become a multi-brand fashion group: it owns global rights to ELLASSAY, Germany's Laurèl and French label IRO (founded by the Bitton brothers in 2005), and runs the UK brand self-portrait in China.
notes: Very private; filings give no biography beyond director/supervisor roles. Husband Xia Guoxin is the public face; route via the securities affairs email. Filings note the controllers hold overseas residency.

name: Li Qinghuai
current_role: Non-executive Director, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 0868)
profile: Li Qinghuai (李清怀; HK filings: LI Ching Wai, aged 68) is one of the founding shareholder group of Xinyi Glass, the auto, float and architectural glass maker started by Lee Yin Yee and fellow Fujian-born auto-parts traders. He joined in April 2001 and has been a non-executive director since 2004, holding ~2.9% directly via his Goldbo International plus a share of the founders' vehicles. Xinyi Glass also owns a large stake in solar-glass maker Xinyi Solar.
interesting_fact: Xinyi Glass's founders, Li included, came from the automobile-parts trading business before moving into making replacement auto glass; the group grew into one of the world's largest glass makers and holds a large stake in Xinyi Solar, a major solar-glass supplier.
deep_cut_fact: His Xinyi Glass shares are held through Goldbo International, a BVI company he wholly owns, and he has sat on the board alongside fellow founders Sze Nang Sze and Li Ching Leung since the 2004 restructuring ahead of the Hong Kong listing.
notes: Chinese name match (李清怀 = LI Ching Wai) is by Hurun listing and Xinyi founder group; Chinese characters were not extractable from the HKEX PDF. Very private, non-executive role; contact via company secretary at ir@xinyiglass.com.hk. Solar-glass link fits an energy show.

name: Frank Torti
current_role: President and Vant Chair, Roivant Sciences (Nasdaq: ROIV); Executive Chair, Immunovant (IMVT)
profile: Dr. Frank Torti, a physician-turned-investor (UNC MD, Harvard MBA), was a healthcare partner at venture firm NEA (2007-18) before joining Roivant in 2018. He oversees Roivant's 'Vant' subsidiaries and was named President in July 2025. His wealth comes from Roivant equity awards, boosted by Telavant's $7.25bn sale to Roche.
interesting_fact: He was the founding CEO and Chair of Roivant subsidiary Telavant from its inception in November 2022 until Roche bought it for $7.25 billion in December 2023, about 13 months later.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he worked at Duke University's Center for Clinical & Genetic Economics (2002-05), doing clinical-trials research and economic evaluations of multinational clinical trials; he later chaired Arbutus Biopharma's board (2018-2025).
notes: Media contact Stephanie Lee and IR contact Keyur Parekh are listed on Roivant's Nov 2026 earnings release. Not a founder, but a good VC-to-operator story.

name: Feng Chunbao
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~34%) of Jikai Equipment Manufacturing (冀凯装备制造, SZSE: 002691); Chairman and GM of Jikai Enterprise Management Group
profile: Feng Chunbao (冯春保) is the Shijiazhuang (Hebei) founder of the Jikai group, whose listed arm makes coal-mine machinery such as roof-bolting drill rigs and tunnelling equipment. He controlled Jikai from its 2012 IPO, ceded control in 2016, regained it in 2018, and holds about 34% (2025 report). He also chairs Australian mining-equipment firms AMM and Unitech Industries.
interesting_fact: His business reaches beyond China: he chairs Australia Mining Machinery Group (AMM) Pty Ltd and Unitech Industries Pty Ltd, and is a director of JK (Thai) Diamond Tools in Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: The group began in diamond tools: Feng was earlier chairman and GM of Shijiazhuang Jikai Diamond Products Co. and a director of Hebei Fushihua Jikai Diamond Tools, and also ran a software firm (Beijing Zhongji Shengke Software).
notes: Jikai's shares are under special treatment (*ST) as of 2026, and there are related-party insolvency proceedings; keep outreach to the mining-equipment and energy angle. Hurun wealth figure (2015-2021) is probably out of date.

name: Zhou Lianqi
current_role: Chairman of the Board (董事局主席), Fujian Septwolves Group; Director, Fujian Septwolves Industry Co. (七匹狼, SZSE: 002029)
profile: Zhou Lianqi (周连期) now goes by Zhou Yongwei (周永伟), aged 64. He and his brothers Zhou Shaoxiong and Zhou Shaoming founded and jointly control Septwolves, the Jinjiang (Fujian) menswear brand known for jackets and casual menswear. He was chairman of the listed company's 2nd board and now chairs the parent Septwolves Group, holding ~2.3% of the listed company directly.
interesting_fact: Septwolves is one of the best-known Jinjiang apparel brands. The three Zhou brothers are joint actual controllers through Fujian Septwolves Group, which Zhou Yongwei chairs.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion he was a banker: deputy director of Bank of China's Jinjing office under the Jinjiang branch. He later earned an EMBA from Xiamen University and is a certified economist (经济师).
notes: Former name confirmed in a Septwolves filing: 周永伟, 曾用名 周连期 (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2020-12-10/1208874824.PDF). In outreach, use the current name Zhou Yongwei. Route via the securities dept email.
